validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real. This is a well-documented Soviet-era North Caucasus gas trunk, built to feed additional gas south into the North Caucasus-Center corridor after the Urengoy-Novopskov (1980-83) and Orenburg-Novopskov (1975) lines filled the Novopskov hub. Confirmed (single-origin family: energybase.ru's listing -- itself blocked behind an access-restriction interstitial on direct fetch, could not be verified live -- mirrored verbatim by uglevodorody.ru and cited as the sole reference by a dedicated uk.wikipedia article) plus GEM's own gem.wiki page and mapped route geometry. Existence is not in doubt (multiple independent listings/mirrors, real named endpoints, plausible corridor route through named Stavropol compressor stations Yegorlyk/Privolnaya/Izobilnaya/Nevinnomyssk/Georgievsk). CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk line (Fuel=Gas is right). DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against all 39 in-scope rows -- no overlap. This line runs SOUTH from the Novopskov hub into Russia (North Caucasus); it does not overlap with the lines that feed INTO Novopskov from the north/east (P0789 Urengoy-Novopskov, P0790 Petrovsk-Novopskov, P0791 Orenburg-Novopskov) or the line heading further into Ukraine (P1483 Novopskov-Shebelinka). No duplicate found.

validity.researcher_notes: Novopskov is a settlement in the NORTH of Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine -- not Russia. GEM's own ResearcherNotes cell on this row already says 'starting point in occupied Ukraine', and CountriesOrAreas already reads 'Russia, Ukraine' (NumberOfCountries=2), but the specific StartCountryOrArea field was never corrected off 'Russia'. Two independent sources confirm the Ukraine location: (1) the dedicated uk.wikipedia pipeline article states the corridor's origin hub is 'газовий хаб у Новопскові (на півночі Луганської області України)' -- 'gas hub in Novopskov (in the north of Luhansk Oblast of Ukraine)' -- and the article itself is categorized under BOTH 'Газопроводи Росії' (Pipelines of Russia) AND 'Газопроводи України' (Pipelines of Ukraine), independently confirming this is a genuinely cross-border line, not wholly Russian; (2) Radio Svoboda (RFE/RL Ukrainian service) -- already cited on this row's own gem.wiki page -- names Novopskov among a list of Starobilsk-raion/Luhansk-Oblast settlements ('Старобільськ', 'Новопсков', 'Біловодськ', 'Мілове', 'Марківка', 'Білокуракине') newly occupied by Russia in 2022 ('вновь захваченных территориях'). These are separate, non-derivative origins on the specific Ukraine-location claim -> tier high.

validity.recommendation: Do not accept 100% Gazprom PJSC ownership as-is on a confirmed cross-border line; flag for a dedicated Update pass to determine an actual split. Not staged as a fill -- no sourced % found, so no replacement value proposed.
validity.researcher_notes: Per the country-standing rule, Gazprom does not own Ukrainian sections of the gas system; on a genuinely cross-border row the correct reading is a split between the Russian-territory owner (Gazprom, for the ~800+ km inside Russia via Aksai/Rostov/Stavropol/North Ossetia to Mozdok) and Ukraine's state gas TSO/MGU structures (for whatever short stretch sits inside Ukrainian territory near the Novopskov hub itself). uk.wikipedia's dual categorization (Pipelines of Russia AND Pipelines of Ukraine) corroborates the cross-border fact underlying this rule. I found no source stating an actual ownership split or percentage, so I am not proposing a replacement Owner value -- only flagging that the current Owner1=Gazprom PJSC 100% is very likely an overstatement and needs Update-level research (e.g., which entity legally holds the Ukrainian-territory segment near Novopskov).

validity.recommendation: Do NOT change LengthKnown=878 off this citation. Flagging the conflict for Update to chase the primary source; the sheet's current 878 km looks more physically plausible than the cited 388 km.
validity.researcher_notes: MATERIAL DISAGREEMENT, but the disagreeing source appears to be the one that's wrong. The only length citation found (energybase.ru's listing -- itself blocked/challenge-walled on direct fetch, so verified only via a Bing snippet and its two derivatives) states the FULL Novopskov-to-Mozdok length is 388 km: uglevodorody.ru mirrors '388 км' verbatim, and uk.wikipedia (whose sole cited reference IS energybase.ru, so not independent of it) states explicitly 'Загальна протяжність газопроводу від Новопскову до Моздоку становить 388 км' -- 'The total length of the pipeline from Novopskov to Mozdok is 388 km.' This is geometrically implausible: I computed the haversine straight-line distance between the pipeline's own two endpoint coordinates -- taken directly from GEM's mapped route file (routes-repo P1471.geojson, RouteAccuracy=high) -- at ~766 km, and the mapped route's own path length sums to ~856 km, closely matching the sheet's existing LengthEstimateKm=856.89 and LengthKnown=878. A continuous pipe cannot be shorter than the straight-line distance between its termini, so a genuine end-to-end Novopskov-Mozdok pipe cannot be 388 km -- whatever '388 km' refers to in the energybase-family record, it is not consistent with the named endpoints as GEM (and the same uk.wikipedia article) locates them. One plausible explanation: a transcription error in the underlying record -- e.g. an original '838 km' with the first two digits transposed to '388' would sit much closer to GEM's 878 and to the mapped-route estimate -- but I could not verify this and am not proposing it as fact, only as a lead for Update. Leaving LengthKnown untouched and Length [ref] UNRESOLVED rather than fill it with a value I have reason to doubt, or overwrite the sheet with an unverifiable citation.

summary: P1471 is a real 1984 Soviet-era North Caucasus gas trunk (Novopskov hub, Luhansk Oblast Ukraine -> Mozdok, Russia); no duplicate found in-scope. Two concerns staged: StartCountryOrArea wrongly reads 'Russia' for the Ukraine-side endpoint (corrected fill, high tier, contradicts GEM's own ResearcherNotes), and Owner=Gazprom PJSC 100% is likely wrong on this now-confirmed cross-border line (flagged, no replacement % sourced).
